minutes.headline: Parks Commission heard four firms pitch Marshall Park master plans; the decision is set for the next Monday meeting.
minutes.summary: The commission interviewed four design firms (Woola, Warner Larson, RDLA and Weston & Sampson) for a Marshall Park master plan, asking each about timeline, ADA and inclusive design, multi-use fields, parking, community meetings and funding sources. No vote on selection was taken; commissioners will grade the interviews and decide Monday. Afterward they discussed the missing project budget, the skate park process, the Marshall Park use dates, soccer nets and the septic design.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the skate park would be self-funded by an outside group, with the town only providing the space.

A firm described Community Development Block Grants, the Community Preservation Act (not yet approved by voters), the Land and Water Conservation Fund and other sources as ways to fund park improvements.
Another firm described state park grants and federal land and water conservation funding, and phasing a project to win successive years of grants.

The chair noted the town has no stated budget for improvements; the assistant town manager said the plan will start big and then be value-engineered, and price proposals were submitted and will be weighed with the ranking.
A firm described phasing a master plan into stages with cost estimates for each so a town can seek grants.

decisions.decision: Commissioners will grade the interviews on the separate interview tab of the scoring sheet and send it to the assistant town manager by Friday.
The selection of a master plan firm will be made by a vote at the Monday regular meeting, with the rankings and costs presented.
Monday agenda to include the skate park, an open space update, the firm decision, a DPW director update and possibly the septic item.
The Monday vote will not authorise the skate park group to start building; a legal agreement process will be clarified later.
The gate behind the 90-foot diamond and the adjacent pipe gate will be closed once the portable toilet is removed.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission interviewed four design firms for a Marshall Park master plan and took no vote on which to hire.
A vote to pick the firm is set for the Monday regular meeting, with rankings and costs presented.
Commissioners will score the interviews on a separate tab of the scoring sheet and send it to the assistant town manager by Friday.
The chair noted the town has no stated budget for park improvements; the assistant town manager said the plan will start large and be value-engineered.
The Monday vote will not authorise the skate park group to start building; the chair said an outside group would fund the skate park.

why_it_matters: The firm chosen will shape what gets proposed for Marshall Park, and with no stated budget the cost to the town, and any later request for tax-funded or Community Preservation Act money, is not yet known.
Firms named grants and the Community Preservation Act, which voters have not approved, as ways to pay, so part of the funding path depends on a vote residents may be asked to take.
